verdicts.rewritten_summary: Outright International country overview (updated 12 Mar 2026): criminalised same-sex intimacy in 2019 (max 6 months + US$8,561 fine), repealed in 2020 after Senate approval — reversal sharply divided public opinion; Nov-2024 constitution (military regime since Aug-2023) codifies privacy (Art.18) but retains Art.16 marriage definition; no legal gender recognition, LGBTI groups cannot register; same-sex relations legal for men and women per its country page (with caveat that criminalisation remains 'No' nationwide only since the 2020 repeal).

Erasing 76 Crimes (25 Nov 2024): Gabon's new constitution was ratified by referendum 16 Nov 2024 (over 90% yes, ~55% turnout) and rejected civil-society demands to re-criminalise homosexuality, adding LGBT+-protective privacy provisions — but codifies a marriage definition excluding same-sex couples. Context: Aug-2023 military coup ended 56 years of Bongo-family rule.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: BBC (10 Dec 2015): States of Guernsey approved same-sex marriage 37-7, rejecting both civil-partnership-only and single 'Union Civile' alternatives; implementing legislation separate and not expected before 2017. Charity Liberate: 'historic day'; debate described as 'extremely positive'.

BBC (24 Jun 2015): Guernsey repealed its 50-year Adoption Law's ban on unmarried couples adopting — States agreed same-sex couples may adopt, with civil partnerships recognised and equal parental responsibility for both partners (Jersey had approved the same change two days earlier).

BBC (23 Sep 2011): Guernsey adopted the UK's relaxed blood-donor rules — gay/bisexual men eligible after 12-month deferral, targeted ~7 Nov 2011 to match the UK change, ending the local 1980s HIV-era ban; other donation restrictions unchanged.

BBC Scotland (19 Jun 2026): Judge Lady Ross ruled the Scottish Prison Service's guidance — allowing some trans prisoners to be held in jails matching their gender identity rather than sex at birth — unlawful; sex segregation in prisons must rest on a lawful basis.

BBC (5 Feb 2026): Court of Session told that housing trans prisoners by sex at birth would breach human rights and create an unacceptable suicide risk; For Women Scotland is challenging the Scottish prison guidance (only biological females in the women's estate), government lawyers defending individual risk assessments as flexible.

The Guardian (17 Apr 2025): British Transport Police amended its strip-searching policy after the Supreme Court gender ruling — trans women to be strip-searched by officers of their sex at birth as an interim position; prior policy had let trans women staff intimately search women holding a GRC; Sex Matters welcomed the change.

Police Scotland (25 Jun 2025): interim guidance on searching transgender persons — searches involving removal of more than a jacket, gloves, headgear or footwear are conducted on the basis of biological sex (custody and stop-and-search); where lived gender differs, efforts will be made to provide an officer of the individual's lived gender on request.

UK Constitutional Law Association analysis (16 Jul 2026) of For Women Scotland v Scottish Ministers [2026] CSOH 59 (Outer House, Court of Session, 19 Jun 2026): critique of the judgment striking down the Scottish Prison Service's non-statutory trans-custody guidance, examining Equality Act 2010 Sch.22(1), the Prison Rules, GRA 2004 and the court's Article 8 approach.

BBC (Aug 2026): new EHRC guidance on single-sex spaces has come into force — the code gives organisations practical examples for compliance (Sex Matters' Maya Forstater: 'the law is clear and the code is practical'); Northern Ireland, on different equality legislation, is still assessing the Supreme Court ruling's impact.

TransActual UK 'Gendered Spaces Report 2025': survey of trans, intersex and gender-nonconforming respondents corroborating their fears of harassment from those opposed to their inclusion in public gendered spaces; full report published as PDF.
JURIST (18 Aug 2026): UN human rights experts warned that UK revisions to the Equality Act 2010 risk discriminating against and excluding transgender people.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Guinea — Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia, LGBTQ rights in Guinea (current): Article 274 of the 2016 Penal Code punishes same-sex conduct with six months to three years' imprisonment, a fine of GNF 500,000–1,000,000, or both; enforcement operates through arrests based on clothing and appearance, releases commonly bought by payment to police, and the law used as a basis for extortion; no legal gender recognition.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: The Advocates for Human Rights UPR stakeholder report on Guinea (Oct 2024): Guinea criminalises consensual same-sex relations while police commit arbitrary arrests, harassment and extortion that deepen stigma and fear; LGBTQ+ people live in a hostile, sometimes lethal environment with threats of physical violence and discrimination on orientation, gender-identity and expression grounds.

BI-FWI (14 May 2025): Guadeloupe's first LGBT+ Centre, the Maison des Diversités et de l'Inclusion, opened 24 April 2024 — a historic first for the island, offering reception, support and orientation for people of diverse identity, sexual, bodily and gender diversities; driven by a federation of Guadeloupean associations.

France-Antilles Guadeloupe: minister Aurore Bergé's visit for the LGBT-centre opening; announced measures to strengthen the fight against gender-based violence and discrimination in Guadeloupe, with adapted structures for overseas territories — the centre's opening cast as a concrete step toward inclusion and safety.

Erasing 76 Crimes (21 Mar 2025): Secret's Out, Queer Gang and Lovo Nova are partnering on a year of LGBT-friendly social events across Guadeloupe in 2025 — described locally as a potential 'annus mirabilis' for the island's community.
